(Currently amended) Claim 1: A system for providing security in a computer system, the system comprising one or more logic circuits, wherein at least one of the one or more logic circuits is configured to: receive a plurality of independent first entropy values from a hardware source; apply at least some of the plurality of independent first entropy values to a function to generate a second entropy value; seed a pseudorandom number generator with the second entropy value; generate a random number using the pseudorandom number generator seeded with the second entropy value; and produce a block of ciphertext or message authentication code using the random number.

(Currently amended) Claim 2: The system of claim 1, wherein the one or more logic circuits is configured to produce the block of ciphertext or message authentication code with a key composed of or derived from the random number.

(Currently amended) Claim 4: The system of claim 1, wherein the hardware source is a ring oscillator, and at least one of the one or more logic circuits is configured to receive the plurality of independent first entropy values from the ring oscillator.

(Currently amended) Claim 5: The system of claim 1, wherein the hardware source is a single hardware source, and at least one of the one or more logic circuits is configured to receive the plurality of independent first entropy values from the single hardware source.

(Currently amended) Claim 6: The system of claim 1, wherein the hardware source comprises a plurality of independent hardware sources, and at least one of the one or more logic circuits is configured to receive the plurality of independent first entropy values from the plurality of independent hardware sources.

(Currently amended) Claim 10: The system of claim 1, wherein the function is a bit-mixer, and at least one of the one or more logic circuits is configured to apply at least some of the plurality of independent first entropy values to the bit-mixer.

(Currently amended) Claim 11: The system of claim 1, wherein at least one of the one or more logic circuits is configured to selectively apply multiple entropy values of the plurality of independent first entropy values to the function to generate the second entropy value.

(Currently amended) Claim 13: A method of providing security in a computer system, comprising: receiving a plurality of independent first entropy values from a hardware source; applying at least some of the plurality of independent first entropy values to a function to generate a second entropy value; seeding a pseudorandom number generator with the second entropy value; generating a random number using the pseudorandom number generator seeded with the second entropy value; and producing a block of ciphertext or message authentication code using the random number.

(Currently amended) Claim 14: The method of claim 13, wherein producing the block of ciphertext or message authentication code includes producing the block of ciphertext or message authentication code with a key composed of or derived from the random number.

(Currently amended) Claim 16: The method of claim 13, wherein the hardware source is a ring oscillator, and receiving the plurality of independent first entropy values includes receiving the plurality of independent first entropy values from the ring oscillator.

(Currently amended) Claim 17: The method of claim 13, wherein the hardware source is a single hardware source, and receiving the plurality of independent first entropy values includes receiving the plurality of independent first entropy values from the single hardware source.

(Currently amended) Claim 18: The method of claim 13, wherein the hardware source comprises a plurality of independent hardware sources, and receiving the plurality of independent first entropy values includes receiving the plurality of independent first entropy values from the plurality of independent hardware sources.

(Currently amended) Claim 19: The method of claim 13, wherein the function is a permutation function, and applying at least some of the plurality of independent first entropy values to the function includes applying at least some of the plurality of independent first entropy values to the permutation function.

(Currently amended) Claim 20: The method of claim 19, wherein applying at least some of the plurality of independent first entropy values to the function includes dividing the plurality of independent first entropy values into multiple groups of independent first entropy values; applying the multiple groups of independent first entropy values to the permutation function to generate permuted groups of entropy values; and concatenating the permuted groups of entropy values to generate the second entropy value.
